problem: Triangle ABC has vertices at A(2, -1), B(5, 3), and C(-1, 4). Determine the length of side AC of the triangle.
subtopic: determining the length of a line segment using the distance formula
solution_steps: Recall the distance formula: d = √((x₂ - x₁)² + (y₂ - y₁)²).
Identify the coordinates of points A and C: A(2, -1) and C(-1, 4).
Substitute the coordinates into the distance formula: d = √((-1 - 2)² + (4 - (-1))²).
Simplify the expression inside the parentheses: d = √((-3)² + (5)²).
The length of side AC is √34 units.

entries.target_teacher_response:
To find the distance between two points on a coordinate plane, you need to use the distance formula. This formula is derived directly from the Pythagorean theorem, which relates the sides of a right triangle. 

If you have two points, $(x_1, y_1)$ and $(x_2, y_2)$, the distance $d$ between them is calculated using the formula:
$$d = \sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2}$$ 

Remember that the distance formula essentially calculates the hypotenuse of a right triangle whose legs are the horizontal and vertical differences between your two points.
